inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in us-east1 runtime pool runtime-g4 (observed 520ms -> 1.2s) at 2026-02-15T14:08:21Z
maya: seeing same in dashboards, heatmap shows a narrow window around 14:06-14:12 UTC
sam: i pulled a flamegraph for a few traces, weird kernel hotpath switching around step 1 of generation
sam: logs: `kernel_select: model=cause-lm-int8, seq=1536 -> selected=generic_fp16_pad`
maya: that matches the kvcache eviction surge we saw earlier — evictions/sec jumped from ~3 -> ~135 in the window
raj: any recent rollout that could change kernel maps or autotune tables?
anya: we rolled a model-variant mapping patch in the router yesterday but it was small (routing weight fix). no kernel runtime changes in prod.
leo: (looking) runtime telemetry shows an increase in small-batched requests at the same time — batch size median dropped from 6 -> 1.5
maya: small batches + long seqlens are a bad combo for our int8 path; runtime falls back to the padded fp16 kernels which are slower and evict kvcache more aggressively
sam: here's the relevant snippet from the runtime profile:
```
# trace snippet
2026-02-15T14:06:07Z kernel_search: candidates=[aot_int8, dynamic_int8, fp16_generic]
2026-02-15T14:06:07Z autotune.lookup(model=cause-lm-int8, seq=1536) -> NOT_FOUND
2026-02-15T14:06:07Z kernel_select -> fp16_generic (pad_seq=2048)
2026-02-15T14:06:07Z kvcache.evict(reason=chunk_pressure, count=42)
```
raj: autotune lookup returning NOT_FOUND is concerning — could be stale shard or missing index after a background compaction?
anya: compaction job did run ~13:50 UTC but finished cleanly. we should still probe the autotune index server logs.
leo: mitigation options: 1) immediate routing override to route heavy seqlen tenants to dedicated-pool, 2) enable conservative-kernel-flag which forces favoring aot_int8 when available, 3) temporarily raise kv_cache_limit per node.
maya: let's do a low-risk route override first for the handful of tenants that show the spike. can we tag by tenant-id?
sam: yes — I have a list of top offenders, sending IDs in DM.
maya: @deploy-bot can you apply a routing override canary for tenant set T{42,87,93} -> dedicated-g4-2 for 5m and observe?
deploy-bot: executing: POST /ops/routes/override {tenants:[42,87,93], target: dedicated-g4-2, ttl:5m} — started (run 1)
leo: also flipping conservative-kernel-flag is quick in config; it's a soft preference, not guaranteed, so low blast radius. should we enable cluster-wide for us-east1?
anya: i'd prefer canary: enable for the affected nodes first. spinning the flag up cluster-wide could mask root cause.
maya: agreed. raj, sam — can you fetch autotune-index logs for 13:45-14:10 UTC? prioritize any ERROR/timeout on lookup calls.
raj: on it. quick check: found repeated timeouts to autotune shard #7 at 14:05:58Z -> 14:07:10Z, approx 120s of intermittent 503s.
sam: that explains NOT_FOUND — fallback path triggered because no autotune response. why did shard #7 flap?
raj: metrics show a GC pause on the indexer process and a concurrent restart event at 14:05:45Z (k8s restart).
maya: root cause looks like autotune indexer restart -> lookups fail -> kernel selection falls back to generic fp16 -> bigger memory pressure -> kvcache evictions -> latency spike.
leo: mitigation summary executed: route override active, conservative-kernel-flag canary on affected nodes, increasing kv_cache_limit by +20% on those nodes.
deploy-bot: conservative-kernel-flag: enabled on nodes [rt-23, rt-24] (canary). kv_cache_limit bumped on nodes [rt-23, rt-24]. routing override TTL 5m.
anya: can we watch p99/evictions over next 10m and then decide whether to roll a broader config change?
sam: adding a short probe that hits seqlen=1536 synthetic traces to confirm kernel selection now prefers aot_int8 on canary nodes.
maya: customer comms: I'll draft an internal blurb for infra->support explaining mitigation and that we're investigating indexer restart.
raj: I'll open an incident ticket with logs and postmortem checklist.
leo: if autotune indexer restarts are frequent, longer-term we should add replica read fallback and cached local copies to avoid lookup-time coupling.
anya: agreed — created follow-up story in backlog: "autotune indexer HA + local caching" (link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2312).
maya: update: after 2m of override, p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 380ms and evictions/sec back to ~5. :thumbsup:
sam: perf probe confirms aot_int8 chosen on canary; latency for synthetic seq1536 traces now ~110ms avg on canary vs 460ms on non-canary.
inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; currently observing normalization in affected pool. Severity: P2 -> monitoring.
leo: leaving this thread open until autotune indexer root cause is confirmed and we've rolled a long-term fix.
maya: thanks all — great quick coordination.
leo: :coffee:
